headlines.title: Man accused of attacking his neighbor with a machete in San Jose
headlines.description: A man was accused of attacking his neighbor with a machete and then barricading himself in his home during a hourslong standoff in San Jose on Sunday, police said. Police said officers responded to the 1800 block of Naples Drive around 9:07 a.m. after receiving a report of a disturbance involving a weapon. The preliminary investigation revealed a man assaulted his neighbor with a machete, according to authorities. The police department said the victim was taken to the hospital and was later released. The victim, Alberto Cuevas, said he’s had other run ins with the same neighbor in the past. He says the assault happened as he went to take his garbage out in the morning. “My wife looked at me. I was crouched down when he struck me. He grabbed me from behind, but I managed to react a little shifting to the side, so he only caught me on the side. Otherwise, he might’ve split my head open,” Cuevas said. “Honestly, you feel afraid and frustrated because there’s nothing you can do and then you are left bleeding.” Cuevas said he received stitches to his head. After the attack, the suspect entered his own home and refused to come out, triggering a standoff. More than seven hours later, police moved toward the home and a man in handcuffs came out, surrounded by officers. Officials said this is an ongoing investigation. Police have not yet released the name of the specific crimes the suspect was arrested for.

headlines.title: ICE agents spotted at San Jose jail, advocates say
headlines.description: Advocates with the Santa Clara County Rapid Response Network said ICE agents were present in the lobby of the Main Jail on Hedding Street in San Jose on Sunday. Advocates responded to the jail in the morning. They said agents were just outside the building as well, apparently waiting for people to be released. On Saturday, members of the same network were at the Elmwood Jail in Milpitas, watching ICE agents there for a third day in a row. Activists want to make it very clear to the agents that their actions are being witnessed and documented. Santa Clara County is a sanctuary county, but no sanctuary policy can prohibit agents from waiting in public areas of the jail. The sheriff’s office says that it does not coordinate with ICE or notify the agency of release dates. They have been tracking ICE visits as well and say agents have been visiting the lobby for more than a year, and taken 60 people into custody who were set for release. NBC Bay Area reached out to ICE for comment on Sunday’s activity but has not heard back.

headlines.title: Santa Clara sets Monday deadline for annual Halloween home-decorating contest
headlines.description: Santa Clara residents have until 5 p.m. Monday, Oct. 26, to enter the city’s annual Halloween Home Decorating Contest, hosted by the Cultural Commission, the city said. The contest is open to city residents and limited to residential properties. Judging will focus on exterior decorations, with entries evaluated on visibility, interactivity, creativity, overall theme and a brief explanation of the decorations, limited to four sentences. Eight winners will be selected: one for the Most Innovative Award, one for Best Group and six district winners, with one from each of the city’s six City Council districts, according to the city. Select Cultural Commission members will judge entries in person by visiting contestants’ homes. Previous winners are not eligible to win the same award two years in a row, although they may qualify for a different category, city officials said. Winners will be announced Friday on the Cultural Commission’s Facebook and Instagram pages. Residents can enter by completing the online entry form here.

headlines.title: Drivers face major detours as Highway 37 in the North Bay closes for the weekend
headlines.description: A portion of Highway 37 in the North Bay remains closed through early Monday morning. The weekend-long closure meant detours for drivers, but Caltrans said the payoff will be worth it. Caltrans shut down the highway Friday night between Mare Island and Sears Point, so crews could do work as part of emergency preparedness for El Niño storm preparation. This weekend, Caltrans focused on median demolition and moving K-Rail to shift traffic. “To move traffic over so that we can complete some work to basically prevent flooding and we want to be able to have this highway open so that when we get our El Niño storms and winter storms, so we can keep this artery open,” Clayton warren with Caltrans said. Caltrans says during the summer, the agency noticed there was some erosion going on in the asphalt, so it had time to plan out how to solve the problem. “We are moving some of the pillars that you see there the K-Rail system to the westbound side and we are going to allow our crews to be able to shore up the road so that we can actually lift portions of the road 3 feet,” Warren said. Work to lift the road will follow. But for drivers this weekend, it meant a long detour to get around the closure.

headlines.title: Man dies and woman is arrested after hit-and-run crash in San Francisco
headlines.description: A man died and a woman was arrested following a hit-and-run crash in San Francisco’s Tenderloin neighborhood early Sunday morning, according to the police department. Police said officers responded to the 800 block of Ellis Street around 1:06 a.m. regarding a crash involving a pedestrian. Upon arrival, officers found an injured man. Authorities said officers rendered aid and the man was taken to the hospital, where he was declared dead. Police said the driver involved had left prior to the officers’ arrival. Through the course of the investigation, authorities said they traced the vehicle’s location to Treasure Island. There, police said the California Highway Patrol had the suspect vehicle stopped for an unrelated traffic violation. Authorities said the female driver was arrested and booked into the San Francisco County Jail on suspicion of homicide.

headlines.title: New partnership aims to reduce whale entanglements in California Dungeness crab fishery
headlines.description: A new partnership of marine scientists, commercial fishermen, and conservationists aims to reduce whale entanglements in California’s Dungeness crab fishery while supporting the state’s fishing industry, a press release issued Thursday noted. The Dungeness Crab and Whale Conservation Collaborative, announced by The Marine Mammal Center, the Pacific Coast Federation of Fishermen’s Associations and The Nature Conservancy, is backed by a three-year grant from the Clean Break Fund. The initiative will combine data from vessel surveys, drones, shore-based observations, underwater acoustic gliders, and satellite-based whale detections to improve understanding of whale movements and behavior. The Marine Mammal Center will lead development of an integrated whale monitoring system, while the fishermen’s association will involve commercial fishers in vessel surveys and entanglement investigations, according to the organization. Meanwhile, the Nature Conservancy will help expand whale monitoring, advance fishing gear recovery technology, and improve the data systems used to guide fishery management. The collaboration will share its findings with the California Department of Fish and Wildlife and other partners to inform the state’s Risk Assessment and Mitigation Program, which helps manage whale entanglement risks, the organization said. Organizers said the effort aims to improve decisions about fishing activity by providing more timely information on whale presence, helping protect marine mammals while supporting fishing communities and sustainable Dungeness crab fishery. Additional partners include Cascadia Research Collective, Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, the Smithsonian Environmental Research Center and Point Blue Conservation Science.

headlines.title: Dog and owner uninjured after fall over Fort Funston cliff
headlines.description: San Francisco Fire Department crews responded to Fort Funston at around 1 p.m. Saturday following a report of a dog that went over a cliff with its owner. Upon arrival, crews confirmed that one dog and one adult were on the cliffside in the shallower section of the cliffs just north of the hang glider deck. While emergency crews were setting up a rope rescue system, the human companion successfully made their way down to the beach below via a dangerous route. Neither the human companion nor the dog sustained injuries. Both were evaluated by emergency personnel and found to be uninjured. The incident has been closed.

headlines.title: Concord police investigate fatal stabbing on Panoramic Drive
headlines.description: A woman was killed and a man was hospitalized in critical condition following a reported domestic disturbance late Friday. At about 8:51 p.m., Concord Police Dispatch received a 911 call regarding a disturbance between a man and a woman at a home in the 2300 block of Panoramic Drive. The caller reported that the man was armed with a knife. Officers responded immediately and spoke with several witnesses. After receiving no response when attempting to contact the home’s occupants, officers forced entry into the residence. Inside, they found a man and a woman injured with apparent stab wounds. Officers administered immediate medical aid prior to the arrival of fire and paramedic crews. Despite lifesaving efforts, the woman was pronounced dead at the scene. The man was transported to a local hospital for medical treatment and remains in critical condition. Detectives from the Concord Police Department Investigations Division assumed the investigation. Investigative follow-up and interviews are underway. Based on preliminary witness information, police stated there are no outstanding suspects and no ongoing threat to public safety. Because the investigation is in its early stages, no additional information is available. Authorities ask anyone with relevant information to contact Det. Justin Wilson at 925-603-5859 or the anonymous tip line at 925-603-5836.

headlines.title: SFFD responds to lithium-ion battery fire on Fell Street
headlines.description: San Francisco Fire Department crews responded to an extinguished lithium-ion battery fire in the 100 block of Fell Street, authorities said Saturday. The fire, which was confined to a single room, produced smoke that prompted several residents to go to balconies, windows, and fire escapes to wait for help, according to the department. All affected residents either sheltered in place or were assisted by firefighters and police officers. No formal rescues were required. Officials noted that the fire was contained quickly due in part to a prompt response by the SFFD and active fire sprinklers. The incident is under control, and no injuries or displacements have been reported, the department stated.

headlines.title: Valkyries beat the Dream 67-62 to even the WNBA Finals at 2-2
headlines.description: Gabby Williams scored 17 points and Golden State played stellar defense to beat the Atlanta Dream 67-62 on Saturday and even the WNBA Finals at 2-2. The best-of-seven series moves back to California on Monday for Game 5. The Valkyries stymied Atlanta star Angel Reese, holding her to just eight points. She had dominated the previous two games, averaging 25.5 points and 14 rebounds in the Dream victories. Reese struggled in Game 4, missing 10 of her 12 shots, including a few layups in the fourth quarter, after having double-doubles in each of the first three games. Atlanta trimmed a 16-point halftime deficit to 61-55 midway through the fourth quarter, bringing fans in the sellout crowd of over 17,000 to their feet. Golden State answered with a 3-pointer by Veronica Burton to briefly silence them. The Dream then scored seven of the next nine points, including a three-point play by Rhyne Howard with 28 seconds left to get within 66-62. Burton then made the first of two free throws a second later and Atlanta couldn’t convert on the other end. Howard finished with 19 points to lead Atlanta. THIS IS A BREAKING NEWS UPDATE. Check back for updates. AP’s earlier story follows below. The Golden State Valkyries are still confident. Trailing 2-1 in the best-of-seven WNBA Finals against Atlanta, they know a win on Saturday will give them back home-court advantage with a trip to “Ballhalla” awaiting. “It would be silly to overreact right now,” Valkyries guard Veronica Burton said. “We continue to point out the things where we lack discipline and where we lack maybe paying attention to their personnel. We address that and not overreact but also understand that there is a major sense of urgency, and we can’t necessarily wait for anything to change.” Still, the Valkyries can ill afford to lose Game 4 after getting routed in Game 3. While it’s only the second year that the WNBA has played a best-of-seven championship series, history in the NBA isn’t on the side of teams trailing 3-1. Only the 2016 Cleveland Cavaliers were able to come back from a 3-1 deficit in the Finals. For the Valkyries to have any chance, they’ll need to find a way to contain Angel Reese. Reese, who was traded to Atlanta from Chicago in the offseason, has made the most of her first postseason appearance since coming into the league three years ago. She became only the second player in finals history with at least 20 points and 10 rebounds in consecutive games, joining A’ja Wilson. At 24 years old, she also became the youngest with three straight double-doubles in the finals. Reese has a really talented group around her in Jordin Canada, Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray, who has been dealing with a hand injury suffered in the semifinals.

headlines.title: Bay Area referee and umpire shortage impacting youth sports
headlines.description: A shortage of referees and umpires is impacting youth sports in the Bay Area. But a South Bay man who will be in the national spotlight and locals hope he will inspire more people to sign up to become officials for amateur sports and address the shortage. Gabe Morales, who graduated from Santa Teresa High School and Santa Clara University before heading off to umpire school, will be the home plate umpire for Friday’s Game 1 of the MLB World Series. For those involved in Bay Area amateur sports, the hope is young people see Morales on one of the biggest stages and be inspired. NBC Bay Area’s Damian Trujillo has more in the video above.

headlines.title: 911 emergency dispatch systems restored in Oakland
headlines.description: Oakland’s 911 system is back up and running as intended following the restoration of the city’s phone service Friday morning. The entire emergency dispatch system for police and fire services went down at about 8:30 p.m. Wednesday after somebody damaged AT&T fiber optic cables in an apparent copper wire theft. The city’s IT teams worked with AT&T to get the computer-aided system and internet back online Thursday evening, but repairs to the phone lines took until Friday morning to complete. During the outage, 911 calls were routed through the Alameda County Sheriff’s Office while OPD dispatchers were relocated to the Oakland Fire Department Dispatch Center and the sheriff’s dispatch center. The Fire Department’s dispatchers were able to handle all fire and medical calls for service and the county was answering 911 calls and relaying information to OPD dispatchers stationed at the Fire Department. The city has contingency plans for just such a situation but “unfortunately both of the initial fallback plans were compromised last night,” Oakland police Chief James Beere said Thursday.
